subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Alex / Tara —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the candid conversation and the clarity on ACME's priorities. Quick recap from our call and the cost levers we discussed so we can align on next steps.

Top pain points you shared:
- Serving costs are spiking with your current approach (estimated 50M tokens/month across customer-facing flows).
- Response latency variability hurts usage-sensitive features (goal: P95 <= 200ms).
- Lack of caching/prefix reuse in the pipeline (lots of repeated context across requests).
- Procurement wants a clear monthly TCO number to compare to current infra spend.

Goals we heard:
- Hit predictable unit economics under $30k/month for inference (pilot target).
- Maintain P95 latency <= 200ms for core features; allow relaxed latency for background batch jobs.
- Run a 60–90 day pilot to validate production metrics and ROI.

Suggested TCO levers (high level):
1) Model selection + token economics
   - Baseline example: For a 13B-like open model, typical hosted token cost (generation + prompt) ranges we showed: ~$0.25–0.45 / 1k tokens depending on batching and quantization.
   - Optimizing to a 7B variant or quantized 13B can move unit cost ~20–40% down.
2) Batching & continuous batching
   - For synchronous requests we can enable micro-batching at the edge (preserving latency SLO) to reduce GPU overhead.
   - For lower-priority flows, we suggested a 50–200ms accept window to increase batch sizes and cut per-token costs by ~15–30%.
3) KV / prefix caching
   - Reuse KV cache for repeated user prompts (e.g., session prefixes) to avoid re-computing early layers — expected 10–25% token reduction on applicable flows.
4) Routing & tiering
   - Route to cheaper model variants for non-critical traffic and keep higher-tier instances for P95-critical requests.
5) Quantization & compilation profiles
   - Use INT8/4-bit quantized variants we validated — small perf hit but large cost improvements on dedicated capacity.

Attached: ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx (workbook with the example calc we discussed) and a short token-cost reference (redwood_token_costs_q1.pdf).

Request / next steps:
- Can you confirm 1) current monthly token estimate (rough), 2) hard latency SLO (P95), and 3) budget guardrail for the pilot ($/month)?
- If those look right, we’ll produce a 2-week pilot plan (scope, success metrics, and a sample billing forecast) and schedule a kick-off.

I’m out Tue morning but free Wed/Thu afternoon — happy to book time.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Marissa —

Great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side after I reviewed with Tara and infra: 

- Token estimate: our best rough number today is ~45–55M tokens/month across the two customer-facing flows (support bot + in-app summarization). We’ll confirm more precisely by EOD Thu.
- Latency SLO: 200ms P95 is a hard requirement for in-app summarization; support bot can tolerate 500ms P95.
- Budget: procurement is looking at ~$30k/month for the pilot, but they want a clear ROI case vs our current self-hosted spend.

On caching: we do have session-level prefixes for the bot but aren’t doing KV reuse across requests — looks like a good optimization to explore.

Can you call out an expected per-token number in the workbook after toggling batching and quantization scenarios? Procurement will want a best / expected / worst case.

If it helps, loop in someone on the infra/devops side for the pilot kickoff — I’ll introduce an engineer after we align on scope.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product — Conversational AI | ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Alex / Tara —

Perfect — thank you for the quick confirmations. I’ll update the attached workbook with a best/expected/worst row that toggles:
- model family (7B vs 13B quantized vs 13B float)
- batching windows (no batching / micro-batching 50ms / batch window 200ms)
- caching enabled vs disabled

And I’ll add an ROI slide that shows monthly savings vs your current self-hosted run-rate (example calc uses your 50M token midpoint).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I’ll update the workbook and share an edited version to the Drive link (expect within 24 hours).
2) We can schedule a 30-minute pilot kickoff next Wed (Apr 7) — bring one infra engineer who owns deployment.
3) If procurement needs a formal SOW/estimate, I can share a pilot SOW template and draft numbers for their review.

If that aligns, I’ll send calendar invites and the updated workbook.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting the pilot running.

Best,
Marissa
